content.overview: BNS s. 348 — Making or possession of any instrument for counterfeiting a property mark.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Making or possession of any instrument for counterfeiting a property mark. BNS restatement of IPC 485. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 485. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 348 is the rule on “Making or possession of any instrument for counterfeiting a property mark”. The section provides that whoever makes or has in his possession any dye, plate or other instrument for the purpose of counterfeiting a property mark, or has in his possession a property mark for the purpose of denoting that any goods belong to a person to whom they do not belong, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 348 exists so that “Making or possession of any instrument for counterfeiting a property mark” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.
